title: Prove P104 transport floor with arbitrary added storage
body:
The P104 side correction still needs at least **96 additional whole-array transports** when arbitrary source-independent workspace lifetimes and arbitrary valid retiming are allowed, provided the original transport occurrences are retained and every cross-frame information transfer is counted.

This extends Jeremy Diviney's PR2113 static-lifetime/retiming cut and David Arias's PR2082 local-excursion floor. Two independently implemented graph checkers collapse every occurrence of the same canonical frame, including separate private lifetimes: all 444 frames partition into 222 source-reachable and 222 target-coreachable frames after removing the same eight original descents. The written factorization proof covers every finite linear program in the stated added-storage model; the certificate checks its exact finite premise.

**Additional transport count is not automatically excess recursive cost.** The package includes a concrete monotone helper path illustrating productive endpoint progress. The inherited `M(0) >= 7659/7592 > 1` comparison is explicitly conditional on unchanged old idle requirements and no new creditable progress. Replacement/fusion of original transports, free cross-chart operations and a changed coverage contract remain outside this result. No attaining correction, admitted supplier or new kappa is claimed.

Only `research/p104-storage-cut/` is added. The README contains the model/proof, cost boundary, predecessor credit and next questions; task/source metadata pins the exact base and inputs; `RESULT.json` contains the complete partition. The scientific base is `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. Contribution commit: `befebf0f4ae7a3f69fe9c5e136262559dcac125f`. Submission overlap covered 381 open PRs and 789 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings, 20:09-20:11 UTC; text matching is not a novelty guarantee. Canonical discussion: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2123.

Validation on CPython 3.12.12:

- Registered package replay passes, with independent reduced-basis versus complete-XOR-span comparison of every transport signature and both full frame sets.
- Six behavior groups pass normally and with `-O`, including actual separation-guard removal, count-preserving partition corruption, equivalent bases, missing/corrupt source and receipt, exclusive output, and read-only source-export replay.
- Exact source/metadata pins, selected-record integrity and staged whitespace checks pass.
- Complex-supplier and exact-circuit-verification specialists independently reviewed the proof and scope. Both were AI-assisted; no human or formal-kernel review is claimed.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-storage-cut
```

No fresh full 280-column scalar identity, native Clifford/phase replay, global owner construction, precision/all-size/outer proof or selected cold replay was run. The frozen native channel is inherited. Hosted CI is separate from these local checks.

Credit Jeremy Diviney/PR2113, David Arias/PR2082, Adam Gall/PR2090/2083/1940, Rohan Arun/PR1972, Chafik Boukhalfa/PR1991 and the geometry/coverage lineage detailed in the README. Discussion2121's replacement joint-side producer remains outside this retained-occurrence theorem. Prepared for Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, verification and prose; Apache-2.0.
